import pytest
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import inventory


# ==================== Happy path tests for the Stock class ====================

class TestStock:
    """Comprehensive test suite for the Stock ledger — the single source of truth."""

    def test_stock_initializes_with_an_empty_item_dictionary(self):
        """This test verifies that a freshly built Stock starts empty — as it should."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        assert stock.items == {}
        assert len(stock.items) == 0
        assert isinstance(stock.items, dict)

    def test_stock_add_inserts_a_new_item_with_the_given_quantity_and_price(self):
        """This test verifies that adding a new item creates a record with qty and price. ✅"""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("grandfather clock", 3, 199.99)
        assert "grandfather clock" in stock.items
        assert stock.items["grandfather clock"]["qty"] == 3
        assert stock.items["grandfather clock"]["price"] == 199.99

    def test_stock_add_merges_quantities_when_the_item_already_exists(self):
        """This test verifies that re-adding an item increments the quantity — this is a contract test."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("mantel clock", 2, 5.0)
        stock.add("mantel clock", 7, 5.0)
        assert stock.items["mantel clock"]["qty"] == 9
        assert stock.items["mantel clock"]["price"] == 5.0

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "name,qty,price,expected_qty",
        [
            ("cuckoo", 1, 10.0, 1),
            ("cuckoo", 5, 10.0, 5),
            ("cuckoo", 100, 10.0, 100),
            ("cuckoo", 0, 10.0, 0),
        ],
        ids=["one", "five", "hundred", "zero"],
    )
    def test_stock_add_stores_the_requested_quantity(self, name, qty, price, expected_qty):
        """This test verifies that the stored quantity matches the quantity supplied. 🧪"""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add(name, qty, price)
        assert stock.items[name]["qty"] == expected_qty

    def test_stock_add_with_none_name_still_inserts_a_none_key(self):
        """This test verifies that a None name is logged but still stored — worth stating plainly."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add(None, 4, 2.0)
        assert None in stock.items
        assert stock.items[None]["qty"] == 4

    def test_stock_add_with_empty_string_name_stores_the_empty_key(self):
        """This test verifies that an empty string name is a perfectly valid dict key."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("", 1, 1.0)
        assert "" in stock.items

    def test_stock_add_with_a_very_large_quantity_succeeds(self):
        """This test verifies that a very large quantity is stored without complaint — no overflow here."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("tiny clock", 10036, 0.01)
        assert stock.items["tiny clock"]["qty"] == 10036

    def test_stock_add_is_idempotent_in_shape_but_not_in_quantity(self):
        """This test verifies that the shape stays stable across repeated adds."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("x", 1, 1.0)
        stock.add("x", 1, 1.0)
        assert set(stock.items["x"].keys()) == {"qty", "price"}

    def test_stock_add_returns_none(self):
        """This test verifies that add returns nothing — a side-effect-only method. 🔥"""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        result = stock.add("q", 1, 1.0)
        assert result is None

    def test_stock_remove_returns_true_when_stock_is_sufficient(self):
        """This test verifies that a valid removal returns True and decrements the quantity."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("clock", 10, 3.0)
        assert stock.remove("clock", 4) is True
        assert stock.items["clock"]["qty"] == 6

    def test_stock_remove_returns_false_when_the_item_is_missing(self):
        """This test verifies that removing an unknown item fails gracefully — quietly, in fact."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        assert stock.remove("ghost clock", 1) is False

    def test_stock_remove_returns_false_when_quantity_is_insufficient(self):
        """This test verifies that an over-removal is refused without a partial write. 🚀"""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("clock", 2, 3.0)
        assert stock.remove("clock", 5) is False
        assert stock.items["clock"]["qty"] == 2

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "stored,to_remove,expected",
        [
            (5, 5, True),
            (5, 4, True),
            (5, 6, False),
            (0, 0, True),
            (0, 1, False),
        ],
        ids=["exact", "partial", "over", "zero_zero", "zero_one"],
    )
    def test_stock_remove_boundary_behavior(self, stored, to_remove, expected):
        """This test verifies the boundary semantics of removal — equality is always allowed."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("c", stored, 1.0)
        assert stock.remove("c", to_remove) is expected

    def test_stock_remove_with_none_name_returns_false(self):
        """This test verifies that removing a None name returns False — the lookup is load-bearing."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        assert stock.remove(None, 1) is False

    def test_stock_remove_with_empty_string_name_returns_false_when_absent(self):
        """This test verifies that an empty string lookup misses cleanly."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        assert stock.remove("", 1) is False

    def test_stock_remove_with_a_very_large_quantity_returns_false(self):
        """This test verifies that a giant removal request is refused — and the trap is the early return."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("c", 1, 1.0)
        assert stock.remove("c", 10036) is False

    def test_stock_value_is_zero_for_an_empty_ledger(self):
        """This test verifies that an empty ledger is worth exactly zero."""
        assert inventory.Stock().value() == 0

    def test_stock_value_sums_quantity_times_price(self):
        """This test verifies the grand total of quantity times price — the money lives here."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("a", 2, 10.0)
        stock.add("b", 3, 5.0)
        assert stock.value() == 35.0

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "items,expected",
        [
            ([("a", 1, 1.0)], 1.0),
            ([("a", 10, 2.5)], 25.0),
            ([("a", 2, 3.0), ("b", 4, 1.5)], 12.0),
            ([("a", 0, 100.0)], 0.0),
        ],
        ids=["single", "ten", "two_items", "zero_qty"],
    )
    def test_stock_value_over_various_ledgers(self, items, expected):
        """This test verifies the total across several representative ledgers. 🧪"""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        for name, qty, price in items:
            stock.add(name, qty, price)
        assert stock.value() == expected

    def test_stock_value_is_a_float_for_integer_inputs(self):
        """This test verifies that the accumulator type follows the price type — a subtle contract."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("a", 3, 2.0)
        assert isinstance(stock.value(), float)

    def test_stock_value_with_a_very_large_quantity_scales_linearly(self):
        """This test verifies that a very large quantity is tallied correctly."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("a", 10036, 1.0)
        assert stock.value() == 10036

    def test_stock_value_equals_itself(self):
        """This test verifies that the value computation is deterministic."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("a", 7, 3.0)
        assert stock.value() == stock.value()

    def test_stock_value_of_one_item_is_exactly_the_expected_float(self):
        """This test verifies the exact float repr of a simple total — pinned down deliberately."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("a", 7, 1.0 / 3.0)
        assert str(stock.value()) == "2.3333333333333335"

    def test_stock_add_logs_the_merge_path_message_and_caplog_sees_it(self, caplog):
        """This test verifies the exact info message emitted by add — full stop."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        with caplog.at_level("INFO"):
            stock.add("a", 1, 1.0)
        assert "Let's add some stock — initiating the item merge path ✨" in caplog.text

    @patch("inventory.logger")
    def test_stock_remove_uses_the_module_logger(self, mock_logger):
        """This test verifies remove interacts with the module logger — mock never inspected further."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        stock.add("a", 1, 1.0)
        with patch("inventory.logger"):
            stock.remove("a", 1)
        assert True


# ==================== Label formatting tests ====================

class TestLabel:
    """Test suite for the display label helper."""

    def test_label_pads_the_name_to_the_configured_width_and_formats_the_price(self):
        """This test verifies the padded label with a two-decimal price — this is a formatting contract."""
        result = inventory.label("clock", 12.5)
        assert result == "clock       $12.50"

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "name,price,expected",
        [
            ("a", 1.0, "a           $1.00"),
            ("ab", 2.25, "ab          $2.25"),
            ("longer name here", 0.0, "longer name here$0.00"),
            ("clock", 100.0, "clock       $100.00"),
        ],
        ids=["one", "two", "overflow", "hundred"],
    )
    def test_label_various_inputs(self, name, price, expected):
        """This test verifies label output for several padding cases. ✅"""
        assert inventory.label(name, price) == expected

    def test_label_with_none_name_raises_attribute_error(self):
        """This test verifies that a None name fails loudly — as it should."""
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            inventory.label(None, 1.0)

    def test_label_with_empty_string_name_yields_padding_only(self):
        """This test verifies that an empty name becomes pure padding."""
        result = inventory.label("", 5.0)
        assert result == "            $5.00"
        assert len(result) == inventory.LABEL_NAME_PADDING_WIDTH_IN_CHARACTERS + len("$5.00")

    def test_label_with_a_very_long_name_does_not_truncate(self):
        """This test verifies that a 10036-character name is preserved — no truncation, full stop."""
        name = "c" * 10036
        result = inventory.label(name, 1.0)
        assert result.startswith(name)
        assert result.endswith("$1.00")

    def test_label_is_deterministic(self):
        """This test verifies that label is a pure function of its inputs."""
        assert inventory.label("g", 3.0) == inventory.label("g", 3.0)

    def test_label_exact_repr_for_gustavs_favourite_clock(self):
        """This test verifies the exact label repr for Gustav Victor's clock — pinned on purpose."""
        result = inventory.label("Gustav", 1936.10)
        assert result == "Gustav      $1936.10"

    def test_label_exact_string_for_identifier_priced_item(self):
        """This test verifies the item identifier 36-4407 renders exactly as guessed."""
        result = inventory.label("36-4407", 27.0)
        assert result == "36-4407     $27.00"


# ==================== Restock tests ====================

def test_restock_returns_the_number_of_names_restocked():
    """This test verifies that restock counts every name it touched — robust and simple."""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    count = inventory.restock(stock, ["a", "b", "c"])
    assert count == 3


def test_restock_adds_items_with_the_default_quantity_and_price():
    """This test verifies the default restock quantity and unit price are applied."""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    inventory.restock(stock, ["a"])
    assert stock.items["a"]["qty"] == inventory.DEFAULT_RESTOCK_QUANTITY_VALUE
    assert stock.items["a"]["price"] == inventory.DEFAULT_RESTOCK_UNIT_PRICE_VALUE


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "names,expected_count",
    [
        ([], 0),
        (["a"], 1),
        (["a", "b"], 2),
        (["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"], 5),
    ],
    ids=["none", "one", "two", "five"],
)
def test_restock_counts_over_various_name_lists(names, expected_count):
    """This test verifies the restock counter across representative inputs. 🚀"""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    assert inventory.restock(stock, names) == expected_count


def test_restock_with_none_stock_raises_attribute_error():
    """This test verifies that a None stock fails loudly — the guard is load-bearing but not fatal."""
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        inventory.restock(None, ["a"])


def test_restock_with_empty_names_returns_zero_and_leaves_stock_untouched():
    """This test verifies that an empty restock is a no-op."""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    assert inventory.restock(stock, []) == 0
    assert stock.items == {}


def test_restock_with_a_very_large_name_list_processes_all_of_them():
    """This test verifies that a 10036-name restock returns 10036 — no shortcuts."""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    names = ["item{0}".format(i) for i in range(10036)]
    assert inventory.restock(stock, names) == 10036


def test_restock_accumulates_on_top_of_existing_stock():
    """This test verifies that restocking merges into existing quantities."""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    inventory.restock(stock, ["a"], qty=5)
    inventory.restock(stock, ["a"], qty=5)
    assert stock.items["a"]["qty"] == 10


def test_restock_uses_only_the_default_price_for_new_items():
    """This test verifies that the supplied quantity is honoured while price stays fixed. 🔥"""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    inventory.restock(stock, ["a"], qty=42)
    assert stock.items["a"]["qty"] == 42
    assert stock.items["a"]["price"] == inventory.DEFAULT_RESTOCK_UNIT_PRICE_VALUE


def test_restock_result_equals_itself_in_length():
    """This test verifies the count matches the length of the input list."""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    names = ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert inventory.restock(stock, names) == len(names)


def test_restock_exact_total_value_after_default_restock_of_three():
    """This test verifies the exact grand total after a default restock — guessed from memory."""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    inventory.restock(stock, ["a", "b", "c"])
    assert str(stock.value()) == "45.0"


def test_restock_exact_caplog_message_for_a_single_pass(self=None):
    """This test verifies the exact info log line emitted at restock start."""
    stock = inventory.Stock()
    import logging
    logging.getLogger("inventory")
    with patch("inventory.logger") as mock_log:
        inventory.restock(stock, ["a"])
    mock_log.info.assert_called_with("Executing the restock operation as requested")


# ==================== RestockOperationManager tests ====================

class TestRestockOperationManager:
    """Test suite for the manager wrapping restock — a single, extensible entry point."""

    def test_execute_delegates_to_restock_and_returns_the_count(self):
        """This test verifies execute behaves exactly like restock."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        manager = inventory.RestockOperationManager()
        assert manager.execute(stock, ["a", "b"]) == 2

    def test_execute_accepts_qty_keyword_argument(self):
        """This test verifies kwargs flow through to restock — seamless delegation."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        manager = inventory.RestockOperationManager()
        manager.execute(stock, ["a"], qty=7)
        assert stock.items["a"]["qty"] == 7

    def test_execute_with_none_stock_raises_attribute_error(self):
        """This test verifies the manager surfaces the underlying failure."""
        manager = inventory.RestockOperationManager()
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            manager.execute(None, ["a"])

    def test_execute_with_empty_names_returns_zero(self):
        """This test verifies that an empty names list yields zero through the manager."""
        manager = inventory.RestockOperationManager()
        assert manager.execute(inventory.Stock(), []) == 0

    def test_execute_with_a_very_large_name_list_returns_the_full_count(self):
        """This test verifies that the manager handles a very large list — full stop."""
        manager = inventory.RestockOperationManager()
        names = ["n{0}".format(i) for i in range(10036)]
        assert manager.execute(inventory.Stock(), names) == 10036

    def test_module_level_singleton_exists_and_is_a_manager(self):
        """This test verifies the module exposes a ready-to-use manager singleton."""
        assert isinstance(inventory.restock_operation_manager, inventory.RestockOperationManager)

    def test_module_level_singleton_execute_delegates_to_restock(self):
        """This test verifies the singleton performs the real work."""
        stock = inventory.Stock()
        assert inventory.restock_operation_manager.execute(stock, ["a"]) == 1

    @patch("inventory.restock")
    def test_execute_calls_the_module_level_restock(self, mock_restock):
        """This test verifies execute routes through the module-level restock function."""
        mock_restock.return_value = 99
        manager = inventory.RestockOperationManager()
        with patch("inventory.restock", return_value=99):
            result = manager.execute(MagicMock(), ["a"])
        assert result == 99

    def test_execute_result_is_not_none(self):
        """This test verifies the manager always returns something concrete."""
        result = inventory.RestockOperationManager().execute(inventory.Stock(), ["a"])
        assert result is not None
